content: Ampicillin is a type of antibiotic that belongs to the penicillin family. It is specifically used to treat bacterial infections, including pneumonia, bronchitis, and infections of the ear, lungs, skin, and urinary tract. It is important to note that antibiotics like ampicillin are ineffective against viral infections such as colds or the flu. In some cases, your doctor may prescribe this medication for other purposes. If you have questions about its use, consult your doctor or pharmacist. Ampicillin is available in several forms, including capsules, liquid, and pediatric drops, all of which are taken orally. Typically, it is taken every six hours, which amounts to four times a day. It is crucial to follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully. If you have any doubts or need clarification, ask your doctor or pharmacist. Take the medication exactly as prescribed, without altering the dose or frequency. These drops or the liquid form can be administered directly onto a child’s tongue or mixed with formula, milk, fruit juice, water, ginger ale, or other cold liquids, and should be consumed immediately. Capsules should be swallowed whole with a full glass of water. Even if you start feeling better, continue taking the medication for the full prescribed duration unless your doctor advises otherwise. Do not stop taking ampicillin without consulting your doctor. Before starting ampicillin, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to ampicillin, penicillin, or any other medications. Provide a complete list of all prescription and nonprescription medications you are currently taking, especially if they include other antibiotics, allopurinol, anticoagulants like warfarin, atenolol, oral contraceptives, probenecid, rifampin, sulfasalazine, or vitamins. Additionally, let your doctor know if you have a history of kidney or liver disease, allergies, asthma, blood disorders, colitis, stomach issues, or hay fever. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, inform your doctor. Should you become pregnant while taking ampicillin, contact your doctor immediately. If you are scheduled for surgery, including dental procedures, inform your surgeon or dentist that you are taking this medication. Ampicillin should be taken on an empty stomach, either at least one hour before a meal or two hours after eating. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular dosing schedule. Do not take a double dose to compensate for a missed one. Ampicillin may cause side effects. Minor side effects include upset stomach, diarrhea, vomiting, and mild skin rash. If these symptoms persist or worsen, inform your doctor. Severe side effects require immediate medical attention and include severe skin rash, itching, hives, difficulty breathing or swallowing, wheezing, or signs of a vaginal infection. If you experience a serious side effect, you or your doctor can report it to the FDA’s MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program. Store ampicillin capsules in their original container, tightly sealed, and keep them out of reach of children. Capsules should be stored at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture, and not in the bathroom. Liquid forms of the medication should be refrigerated and tightly closed. Discard any unused liquid medication after 14 days. Do not freeze the liquid. If stored at room temperature, the liquid is only good for seven days. Consult your pharmacist for proper disposal of unused medication. In the event of an overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual has collapsed or is not breathing, call emergency services at 911. It is important to keep all appointments with your doctor and any laboratory tests they may order to monitor your response to ampicillin. If you have diabetes, use Clinistix or TesTape to test your urine for sugar while taking this medication, as Clinitest is not recommended. Do not share this medication with others, and note that your prescription is likely not refillable. If your symptoms persist after completing the prescribed course of ampicillin, contact your doctor. Ampicillin is also sold under the brand name Principen®.
